messages:
maya: hey folks — first day. running the dev stack with colima + docker compose and my app can't reach Postgres. db container says "Up" but app error is "could not connect to server: No such file or directory" (looks like socket issue)

taylor: do you have `platform: linux/amd64` in your compose? that can weirdly break colima on arm chips

maya: no platform set. here are the quick outputs:

maya: ```
$ docker compose ps
NAME   IMAGE          COMMAND                  STATE      PORTS
db     postgres:15    "docker-entrypoint..."   Up (healthy)
```

maya: and `docker logs db` ends with `database system is ready to accept connections`

jake: if Postgres says ready but client gets "No such file or directory" it usually means the client tried the unix socket path while Postgres is only reachable over TCP. what's your DATABASE_URL?

maya: uhhh `postgres://postgres@/mydb` — so no host, lol

maya: changed to `postgres://postgres@localhost:5432/mydb` and now app errors with `FATAL: could not create lock file "./pgdata/postmaster.pid": Permission denied`

taylor: volume ownership issue. colima tends to map things differently. try `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` (postgres user in image is 999) or set `user: "postgres"` in compose for the db service

maya: ran `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` and restarted — postgres comes up but migrations fail: `ERROR: could not access file "$libdir/pgvector"` when trying to create extension pgvector

sam: pgvector needs to be present in the server image. either use an image with pgvector baked in (e.g. `ankane/pgvector:postgres15`) or build a custom image that installs `pgvector` before init.

maya: switched to `image: ankane/pgvector:postgres15` and init now succeeds. everything looks green locally. thanks all!

infra-bot: FYI — internal dev-setup doc updated with colima notes: https://go.redwood/dev-setup (:book:)

maya: adding to my onboarding notes — maybe we should include a tiny checklist: 1) ensure DATABASE_URL has host, 2) chown pgdata to 999:999 for colima, 3) use pgvector-enabled image or build image. tagging @taylor for docs follow-up :pray:
